summary.one_liner: A text outline of a Go developer learning roadmap, listing the topics, tools and libraries a Go developer might study next, from prerequisites to microservices.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a roadmap in list form: a bulleted and numbered outline grouped into 15 sections such as prerequisites, CLI tools, web frameworks and routers, databases, ORMs, caching, logging, real-time communication, API clients, testing, task scheduling, microservices and Go patterns. Each section names libraries or products, for example cobra and urfave/cli for CLI tools, Gin, Echo and Fiber for web frameworks, and Zap, ZeroLog and Logrus for logging. The page says the chart is meant to show the landscape, not to push trendy tools. It links to translated versions of the README. The chart itself is a Draw.io diagram and is not described in the text. The README has no install or run steps.
use_cases: Deciding what to learn next as a Go developer
Comparing Go ORMs and database drivers
Picking Go logging or testing libraries
Getting an overview of Go microservice tools
stack: Draw.io (used to build the roadmap diagram)
notable: Covers 15 topic areas from prerequisites through microservices and Go patterns
Lists the Go libraries and tools for each topic, such as Gin, Gorm and gRPC-Go
Includes a disclaimer that hype does not always mean the best fit for a job
Offered in several translations, including Chinese, Japanese, Portuguese, Korean, Russian, Ukrainian and Arabic
caveats: The README is a topic list, not a tutorial, and gives no detail on each tool
The title says 2021, so some listed projects may be outdated
The Go-Patterns section is empty in the README
